description:
From: Elixir Parity. Approved by the user 2026-11-24 (relayed by Elixir Parity). Page: ../fz-module-atom-identity.html. Research notes: Elixir Parity's scratchpad rmod/notes.md, with Elixir probes p1.exs and p4.exs.

Today (Elixir 1.19.4 probed vs fz):
- `defimpl A, for: B.C`: in Elixir its module is Module.concat(A, B.C), the atom A.B.C. In fz it is a separate ProtocolImpl{A, B.C} identity whose atom is also A.B.C.
- That impl, plus `defimpl A.B, for: C`, plus a real `defmodule A.B.C`: Elixir has one module, redefined twice ("redefining module A.B.C"). fz has three distinct modules, a boundary documented in protocols.md:43-58.
- Calling the atom A.B.C, or apply(A.B.C, ...): in fz this always reaches the real A.B.C, and no atom reaches the impl.
- __MODULE__ inside an impl is the display atom, which as a call target decodes to the real A.B.C, while __CALLER__.module in the same spot means the impl (env_projection.rs:62-76).
- env.module is an alias node that carries the identity in hidden metadata (__fz_module__). Atoms already resolve without aliases (quoted_function.rs:1914).

Fix:
- An impl module is Named(Module.concat(protocol, target)), so a module's identity is its name and its name is its atom. Protocol dispatch keys on module ids and does not change.
- env.module and __MODULE__ are the plain atom; __MODULE__ and __CALLER__.module become one value.
- A second definition of a module name warns "redefining module X" through fz-mue.32's warning channel and keeps the later one in source order (the user's decision).
- protocols.md's three-owner boundary is retired in favour of Elixir's single atom.

Removal ledger (this ticket; about 28 files):
- The ProtocolImpl denotation, so ModuleDenotation collapses into ModuleName.
- The __fz_module__ alias metadata, quoted_parts and display_segments.
- Expr::Module, and the Exact / Unresolved module-target split for atoms.
- The alias branch of project_module_value.
- AOT carrier tag 2 (function_denotation.rs:161, 268).
- env.module as an alias node dies in fz-mue.51 commit 1.

Done when:
- An oracle fixture covers `defimpl A, for: B.C`: calling through the atom and through apply/3; __MODULE__ == __CALLER__.module inside an impl's macro use; Atom.to_string and inspect of an impl module; the Decoy alias case. It matches Elixir on run, interp and build.
- A redefinition fixture shows the warning.
- Fixture 01574 is rewritten: it keeps the Decoy alias case, and drops the three-owner collision and its self_val_after_display_edit macro (which would raise MatchError in Elixir).
- The three-owner unit tests (source_publish_test, scope_test, source_test, quoted_function_test, semantic_analysis_test, drive_test:2793) are rewritten to claim one atom, one module.
- Work pins fall or stay flat; any rise comes to the user with its probe.

Build notes (Elixir Parity, 2026-11-24): the redefinition warning goes through the ordinary compiler warning path (code resolve/module-redefined), not IO.warn, so fz-mue.32 is not a blocker. ModuleTarget::Exact survives, now holding a ModuleName: it is the only thing keeping an unquoted module atom out of lexical alias resolution (the Decoy case).
title: A module's atom is its identity: defimpl P, for: T is the module P.T, as in Elixir
